audits.title: Audit of referral of diabetic patients.
audits.standard: National target for referral and feedback from the eye clinic
audits.setting: Wasat Abha Primary Health Care Center, Aseer region
audits.other_findings: Rates remained below the national target; prevalence of diabetic retinopathy 11.3%. No intervention between years is described.
audits.citation: Al-Khaldi YM, Khan MY, Khairallah SH. Audit of referral of diabetic patients. Saudi Med J. 2002;23(2):177-181. PMID: 11938394.

audits.title: Use of collaborative audit to assist local implementation of the SIGN guideline for prevention of visual impairment in diabetes.
audits.standard: SIGN guideline for prevention of visual impairment in diabetes (annual eye review and risk factor monitoring)
audits.setting: Two district general hospitals and 59 of 63 general practices, Ayrshire and Arran Health Board

cycle1.result: Dilated fundoscopy within one year 72%; visual acuity 69%; HbA1c recorded 85% (65% of these 8% or less); BP recorded 88% (52% at or below 140/90); smoking status 89%.

audits.other_findings: Only 83% of practices had near vision testing equipment and 54% a pinhole occluder.
audits.citation: McCarlie J, Alexander G, Sommerville J, McGettrick P, MacPherson N, Collier A. Use of collaborative audit to assist local implementation of the SIGN guideline for prevention of visual impairment in diabetes. Health Bull (Edinb). 1999;57(1):29-34. PMID: 12811862.

audits.title: Diabetic retinopathy screening in New Zealand requires improvement: results from a multi-centre audit.
audits.standard: National diabetes retinal screening guidelines (referral and review within six months)
audits.setting: Four main centre retinal screening services

cycle1.result: 75 (48%) referred to ophthalmologist as recommended; 45 (60% of referred) seen within six months.

audits.other_findings: Recommended dataset incomplete; screen-positive proportion varied 1.2% to 3.4% between centres.
audits.citation: Hutchins E, Coppell KJ, Morris A, Sanderson G. Diabetic retinopathy screening in New Zealand requires improvement: results from a multi-centre audit. Aust N Z J Public Health. 2012;36(3):257-262. doi:10.1111/j.1753-6405.2012.00841.x. PMID: 22672032.

audits.title: Barriers to Yearly Diabetic Retinopathy Screening Attendance: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: NICE annual diabetic eye screening for patients aged 12 and over; NHS DES uptake target 75%

cycle1.result: DES uptake 77.2% (n=465) for the 15-month cohort and 83.6% (n=503) for the 36-month cohort, exceeding the 75% target.

audits.other_findings: Survey of non-attenders cited mental health issues, lack of awareness and transport difficulties; telephone prompts, text reminders and online education proposed but not re-audited.
audits.citation: Chanda UL, Madasu A, Bhardwaj A, Mohyudin M. Barriers to Yearly Diabetic Retinopathy Screening Attendance: A Retrospective Clinical Audit. Cureus. 2024;16(12):e75474. doi:10.7759/cureus.75474. PMID: 39791053.

audits.title: Improving Timely Annual Ocular Examinations for Patients With Diabetes Mellitus in a Primary Care Office.
audits.standard: American Diabetes Association guideline for annual ocular examination; target 85% within 90 days

cycle1.result: 48% of patients with diabetes had an annual ocular examination.

audits.intervention: Four PDSA cycles: team huddles and training, diabetes education checklist, EMR checklist and logbook referral tracking.

cycle2.result: 86% had annual ocular examinations; 87% of referred patients completed the appointment.

audits.citation: Park S. Improving Timely Annual Ocular Examinations for Patients With Diabetes Mellitus in a Primary Care Office. J Nurs Care Qual. 2021;36(3):274-278. doi:10.1097/ncq.0000000000000508. PMID: 32826697.
